_about: Bundled schematic review checklist of altium-copilot (run_review_checklist). Item texts are this project's own words; the topics follow Altium's schematic review checklist (resources.altium.com/p/schematic-review-checklist). Teams change it with review_checklists.json (see README).
title: Schematic review
description: Power, signals and interfaces, components and ratings, connectors and protection, testability and production, style and documentation.
source: Topics after Altium's schematic review checklist (resources.altium.com/p/schematic-review-checklist); items written for this project.

items.text: Every power rail is fed by something: a regulator, a power input, a battery or another rail.

no.label: rails with loads and no source

judge.label: rails with no source found (a pin the part regulates itself, or fed from off the board)

items.hint: The power tree is read from names: a rail fed through a part it does not recognise looks unfed.

items.text: Regulator enable pins are tied, pulled or driven, and none is held off by mistake.

judge.label: enable notes

items.hint: Check each EN pin's polarity and internal pull in the converter's datasheet.

items.text: Each adjustable regulator's feedback divider sets the output voltage the rail is meant to have.

no.label: feedback dividers that set another voltage than the rail's

judge.label: dividers implying an uncommon reference voltage
converters whose output rail is unknown

items.hint: Recalculate with the datasheet's reference voltage (get_power_tree vref=).

items.text: Power entering the board is protected against over-current, reverse polarity and transients as the product needs.

no.label: external power inputs with no fuse
external power inputs with no reverse-polarity protection
external power inputs with no TVS or clamp

judge.label: input protection notes (inputs of unknown exposure)

items.hint: Whether a fuse or TVS is needed depends on the source (a bench supply, a vehicle, a cable).

items.text: Switching regulators have their input and output capacitors, and an input filter where their noise matters.

judge.label: converters with no input or output capacitor found
switching regulators with no input filter

items.hint: The power tree reports these as notes: a capacitor behind a ferrite or on a differently named net is not seen, so check each converter on its sheet.

items.text: Power-good signals and the start-up order of the rails are used as the parts' datasheets ask.

judge.label: power-good and sequencing notes

items.hint: FPGAs, processors and DDR memory often need a rail order: compare with their datasheets.

items.text: Every IC supply pin has a fitted decoupling capacitor on its own rail.

no.label: IC rails without a fitted capacitor

judge.label: decoupling notes

items.hint: The datasheet decides how many capacitors each supply pin needs and of what value.

items.text: Capacitors keep a safe margin between their voltage rating and the voltage across them, and small ceramics keep enough capacitance under DC bias.

judge.label: capacitor rating notes
rails without a known voltage (pass rails=)

items.hint: Confirm ratings in the datasheets; give the voltages of rails whose names carry none (check_derating rails=).

items.text: Resistors stay within their power and working-voltage ratings, and the currents of LEDs and shunts are known.

judge.label: resistor notes and currents to look up

items.text: Parts that dissipate power stay below their maximum junction temperature with margin.

no.label: parts above their maximum junction temperature

judge.label: parts near their maximum junction temperature
hot parts whose dissipation needs loads or efficiencies

items.hint: Loads, efficiencies and thermal resistances come from the datasheets and the user (check_thermal load=, theta=).

items.text: The offline ERC finds no errors or fatal errors.
items.hint: run_erc approximates Altium's ERC: confirm with Project > Validate PCB Project in Altium.

items.text: Connectivity warnings (floating labels or power ports, loose wires, single-pin nets, ports or sheet entries without a match) are fixed or intended.

violation: Port not linked to parent sheet symbol
Sheet Entry not linked to child sheet

judge.label: wire ends that almost touch

items.hint: An intended one wants a No ERC marker or a level change, not a redesign.

items.text: Reset, enable, boot, strap and open-drain lines have a defined level: a pull resistor or a driver.

judge.label: pull resistor notes

items.hint: Pulls inside ICs are invisible here: check the datasheet before calling one missing.

items.text: I2C pull-up values suit the bus speed and its capacitance.

no.label: I2C buses with an unsuitable pull-up

judge.label: I2C pull-up notes
I2C buses not judged ok

items.hint: Ask the bus speed and pass check_pull_resistors i2c_mode= and bus_capacitance_pf=.

items.text: Signals between ICs on different supply rails have compatible logic levels, and no input is driven above its supply.

judge.label: logic level notes and rails of unknown voltage

items.hint: Confirm VOH, VIH, 5 V tolerance and absolute maximum ratings in both datasheets.

items.text: Dividers, LED and optocoupler currents and ADC input filters compute to the intended values.

na.label: no divider, LED, optocoupler or filter found

judge.label: calculation notes
rails whose voltage is needed (pass rails=)

items.hint: Vf, Vref and thresholds are datasheet values: recheck each calculation with them.

items.text: The processor's UART, boot and strap pins are wired as intended: TX meets RX, boot levels are set.

na.label: no processor, FPGA or radio found

judge.label: pin notes

items.hint: Check pin functions and boot modes against the processor's datasheet.

items.text: The sheet hierarchy is consistent: sheet symbols point at existing sheets, and entries and ports match.

judge.label: hierarchy warnings

items.text: Differential pairs and other critical nets are named and marked (diff-pair directives, net classes) as the layout needs.

no.label: directives that did not reach the board, or differ there

judge.label: directive notes (left out by Class Generation, a Constraint Manager project, board items no directive gives)

yes.label: pairs, net classes or rules marked by schematic directives reached the board

items.hint: Which nets need a pair or a class is the designer's call; check_directive_sync says whether those marked reached the board (list_diff_pairs and get_classes list them).

items.text: Designators are unique and every part is annotated.
Every placed part's symbol and footprint are found in a library the project uses.

no.label: parts whose library item is not found

judge.label: library notes (Workspace or database parts are not readable offline)

items.text: The symbols used pass the library rule check: pins named and numbered once, description, designator prefix and footprint set.

judge.label: symbols without a description or footprint

items.text: Every BOM part has a footprint and a real description, not a placeholder.

no.label: parts without a footprint or with a placeholder text

judge.label: description notes

items.text: Each IC follows its datasheet's application circuit: pin functions, required external parts, unused pins handled.
items.hint: Read each IC with get_sheet_context and its datasheet; name any part without a datasheet.

items.text: Polarised parts (diodes, LEDs, electrolytic and tantalum capacitors) and transistors are connected the right way round.
Parts are rated for the product's temperature range and environment, and safety-relevant parts carry the approvals they need.
Pins of connectors the outside world can touch have ESD or TVS protection near the connector.

judge.label: ESD notes (connector exposure unknown or internal)

items.hint: Confirm which connectors are user-facing (check_interfaces external= / internal=) and the TVS part's ratings.

items.text: Cable shields and connector grounds are tied as intended: no floating shield, no ground only through a part by accident.

judge.label: shield and ground notes

items.text: Low-speed lines leaving the board have a place for a series resistor or ferrite, for EMC tuning.

judge.label: off-board lines with no series element

items.text: Connector pinouts match the mating connector, cable or board, and pin 1 and keying are documented.
Inputs from the outside world survive miswiring, overvoltage and hot-plugging as far as the product requires.
The processor can be programmed and debugged: its debug and boot pins reach a header or test pads.

na.label: no processor, FPGA or radio found

no.label: debug or programming pins without access

judge.label: debug access notes

items.text: The project files are sound: no missing documents, legacy file types, stale variant entries or hidden characters in names.

judge.label: integrity warnings

items.text: ERC settings keep Altium's important checks on, and each No ERC marker hides only an intended violation.

judge.label: No ERC markers on power or multi-pin nets
ERC checks switched off that can hide faults
relaxed Connection Matrix cells

items.text: Rails and signals the test plan measures have test points or reachable pads.
items.hint: check_testpoints shows probe access on the board.

items.text: Not Fitted parts and variant choices are explained (why a part is left out, which variant ships).
Title blocks give the same revision and date on every sheet and drawing.

judge.label: title block gate warned or not verified

items.text: Objects sit on the grid and inside the sheet border.

violation: Object not completely within sheet boundaries

judge.label: off-grid or off-sheet objects

items.text: Each rail has one name and power ports are used consistently.

judge.label: nets with several names
rail aliases and name casing

items.text: Sheets read clearly: signals flow from inputs to outputs, related circuits are grouped, net names say what the net carries.
Design notes explain the non-obvious: chosen values, Not Fitted parts, open questions.
items.hint: get_design_notes lists the notes of every sheet and drawing.
